=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope note:** I reviewed only the Seller's cover note, Seller Update and Disclosure Letter as provided. I have not checked the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents or the full draft SPA. The data room is indexed as at 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026, so the position needs a bring-down before signing. Final sign-off should come from NSW-qualified counsel.

**Priority:** Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), employee bonuses (AUD 420k), Ironquay (AUD 180k) and Sandbar (AUD 330k) are debt-like or price items. Under a debt-free/cash-free price they should come off the price through the funds flow, not sit inside warranty claims.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** General warranty claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap (e.g. 30%, AUD 7.2m), with known matters, fundamental warranties, tax and fraud carved out of it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30% and carve out the rest. *The cap level matters less than the Seller's proposal to sweep every claim type under it.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis per claim; AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of about AUD 10k; a tipping basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%) so the whole claim counts once the threshold is passed; related claims aggregated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket. *A deductible of AUD 250k removes the first loss entirely, and a tipping basket makes the whole claim recoverable.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general warranties, applied to all claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months, so that a full post-Completion audit cycle and year-end have passed.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months. *18 months may expire before the first full-year accounts and tax position can reveal a pre-Completion issue.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) capped at price, outside the de minimis and basket, with a limitation period of at least six years (NSW Limitation Act 1969 contract period, to be confirmed by counsel).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *The buyer is purchasing title to 100% of the shares, and a AUD 4.8m cap on that is unacceptable.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No express fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** Express exclusion of fraud and wilful concealment from all caps, time limits, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance and buyer-knowledge provisions.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out. *The Seller's drafting would otherwise purport to exclude fraud claims, so the carve-out needs to be express.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, made fairly and against a specific warranty. Data room and public register disclosure excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure. *Disclosing the whole data room would effectively remove most warranty protection.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Clause 8.3 deleted, plus a pro-sandbagging clause confirming the buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge. Known issues handled through specific indemnities and price adjustments.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 8.3 and add the pro-sandbagging clause. *The buyer now knows of DD-002 to DD-012 issues, and 8.3 would remove recourse for the risks most likely to crystallise.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DD-002 records about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (about 30%). Final consent and evidence of the clause 11.3 conditions are not in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A hard condition precedent to Completion: final written consent with clause 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced. Buyer-only right to waive. Termination right if not obtained, or a price adjustment if consent is conditional.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a hard condition precedent. *About 30% of revenue depends on this consent, and "reasonable endeavours" gives no certainty.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at Completion from the price (debt-free mechanics), with a payout letter, discharge of security under clause 9.2, PPSR discharge, and any change-control consent under clause 8.1 obtained.
- **Recommendation:** Pay out and discharge at Completion through the funds flow. *A post-Completion release leaves the company the buyer is acquiring exposed to a AUD 3.2m secured lender.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses, not in the funds flow, described as "a matter for the Seller". Employer on-costs not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** Treated as Seller-borne debt-like items deducted from price, including payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, paid through payroll at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct from price with on-costs included. *Under debt-free/cash-free pricing these are seller liabilities, and the buyer would otherwise pay them after Completion.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and described as adequate. DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, which is not bank-verified. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Evidence of payment or the AUD 180k deducted as debt-like. Confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials delivered at Completion. A specific indemnity for IP ownership defects and related third-party claims, outside the cap and basket. IP ownership warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Require payment or a deduction, plus assignment and a specific IP indemnity. *The company may not hold title to the Project Materials it relies on until payment is verified, and the Seller's indemnity covers only the fee itself.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Described as preliminary and not expected to be material. DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external address, with about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligations are unresolved, and no loss is quantified.
- **Buyer should want:** A forensic investigation before signing, or as a condition. Assessment of whether the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies, including whether the company is an APP entity. A specific indemnity covering notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party costs, outside the cap and basket with a longer time limit. A data-security and breach-history warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain a pre-Completion investigation and a specific indemnity. *Personal information of about 1,240 people has unknown access, and the Seller's characterisation is not an adequate basis for risk allocation.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k, described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008 and DD-011 are to be read together for timing and scope.
- **Buyer should want:** Review of contract terms, term, termination rights and change-of-control provisions. Any prepaid or non-terminable amounts treated as debt-like or adjusted through working capital.
- **Recommendation:** Verify the contracts and treat non-ordinary or prepaid amounts as debt-like. *The Seller's description is unverified, and the disclosure does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable or terminable.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime (caps, basket, 18 months, knowledge and disclosure rules) applies to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities (known issues) and fraud, each with its own cap, time limit and exclusions.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *It would subject title and tax risk to the same limits as ordinary operating warranties.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, which records Harbourglass as holder of 100%. No buyer verification is recorded.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before signing: ASIC company extract, inspection of the register and constitution, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation the Riverlark security does not cover them, and board and transfer documents. Delivery of share certificates and executed transfers at Completion, and a title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent searches before signing. *A seller-prepared register is not verification, and title to the shares is the asset being bought.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions described as "settled under the general regime", meaning the caps, basket and 18-month limit apply.
- **Buyer should want:** Standalone tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, capped at price, with no basket and a limitation period matching the ATO assessment period (at least six years). Separate IP warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Tax liabilities can crystallise after 18 months, and the tax and IP diligence is not complete.*

---

**Next steps:** (1) Bring down the data room to the current date. (2) Confirm the Completion funds flow treats Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay and any Sandbar debt-like amounts. (3) Table the hard conditions for Bluefen and title verification. (4) Prepare the specific indemnity schedule covering Ironquay, the privacy incident, tax and Sandbar.
